label: sparse mixed context (weak bias toward n-initial sequences, mid-sequence)
explanation: Very sparse (0.026% of steps), never fires at t<3. Activations are split almost evenly between the original phase (mostly t=4-6) and the copy phase (mostly recall_idx 2-4). There are weak enrichments: first token n (8.8x lift, 30% of mass), in_tok v/q/p, prev_tok j/r/i/d, out_tok n/y, and next_out n/s/w. Top examples are original-phase steps in n-initial, digit-free sequences where p/v/d is input after r/i/d. But every predicate built from these has precision below 6% and F1 below 0.08. The best one, n-first + prev_tok in {j,r,i,d,x} + in_tok in {p,v,q,d,w}, gets dev P=0.055, R=0.12. Copy-phase activations near an upcoming n output also have very low precision. Magnitude is narrow (median 0.12, max 0.24), and the highest activations sit in n-initial sequences during the original phase. No coherent description found.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=r (+2.99), orig0=n (+2.95), prev_tok=j (+2.93), out_tok=n (+2.84), phase=0 & in_tok=p (+2.84), prev_tok=i (+2.74). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-4.55), to_go=8 (-3.10), in_tok=s (-2.81), prev_tok=w (-2.76).
